notes: Summary: Helmbridge is a programmatic advertising platform evaluating Redwood Dedicated for low-latency auction-time inference (RTB). Primary ask: legally guaranteed sustained throughput + well-defined burst allowances for bidding spikes.
Business drivers: reduce lost bids during peak auctions, consolidate model serving across regions, lower cost/unit vs. cloud-managed GPUs.

Workload profile: mix of small-chat style assistant (latency-sensitive) + heavy reranking for candidate lists + embeddings for similarity. Peak auction windows create short, intense bursts (10-60s) several times per minute during campaign hours.
Throughput ask (negotiation):
- Minimum sustained tokens/sec: 50,000 tokens/sec across US-east cluster (for 4 model shards of the bidding model).
- Concurrency cap: target support for 1,200 concurrent short-lived sessions (per-instance planning uses session multiplexing).

- Burst policy: allow up to 150,000 tokens/sec for bursts up to 45 seconds at 2x/month without penalty; beyond that, soft throttling or queued bursts acceptable.  Customer requests explicit bursting formula in SOW.
- Warm pool requirement: pre-warmed KV caches for top-1000 advertisers per shard to avoid cold-start latency during burst windows.

Latency/SLAs: p95 generation latency target < 120ms for 16-64 token requests under normal sustained load; want carve-outs for catastrophic failures. Interested in SLO definitions, measurement windows, and credits (minutes vs. token-based refunds).
Reserved GPU planning:

- Preferred hardware: H100 class for quantized FP16 workflows; open to A100 if pricing delta warrants. Initial reserve ask: 8 H100 equivalents in US-east; plan to scale to 16 after Q3 if traffic model validated.
- Autoscale/burst model: want predictable reserved baseline (90% guarantee) with burst capacity on-demand at pre-negotiated unit cost and guaranteed preemption rules.

Security/compliance notes: require SOC2 Type II evidence before go-live; SSO via SAML, KMS integration for key rotation, audit-log shipping to Splunk. Data residency rule: bidding logs stored in US only for EU/US segmentation.
Timeline & activities:
- 2026-01-18: Intro call — product fit, initial throughput numbers collected (fireflies ff_20260212_8321 reference).
- 2026-02-05: Architecture deep-dive with infra and model ops (SE Priya). Reviewed KV cache plan and sharding approach.

- 2026-02-26: POC planning meeting — Helmbridge agreed to 4-week POC using 2 reserved nodes + burst allowances; metrics to collect: sustained tokens/sec, p95 latency, tail Q99 latency, cost/unit.
- 2026-03-02: Procurement/Legal raised two main items: SLA credit language (pro-rata vs. fixed credit) and burst overage pricing model. Drafting redlines.
POC acceptance criteria (customer-specified): sustained 48k tokens/sec for 1 hour test window with p95 < 140ms; no more than 5% error/timeout rate during spikes; predictable billing for bursts.
Quote & negotiation notes:
- Customer pushed back on 99.9% uptime SLA without explicit warm pool guarantee — asks for 99.95 for core auction path.
- Wants committed minimum tokens/sec written into contract (with step-down schedule tied to usage) and a transparent formula for credit calculation when Redwood misses throughput SLOs.
- Interested in an A/B fallback policy: if primary dedicated pool saturates, route to a smaller hosted model with a defined latency delta and cost cap. Need explicit routing SLA.
Open questions for Redwood team:
- How is batching accounted for in sustained tokens/sec? Do we accept aggregated batch token throughput or per-request token billing for guarantees?
- Can Redwood provide a documented burst window policy (duration, frequency, gradual ramp) that we can include in SOW?
- Can we reserve exact GPU SKUs and guarantee placement (no GPU sharing with other tenants) or only capacity equivalents?
